mainTopic: Drinking and carrying between domains: the winepress, gutters and pipes, cisterns and garbage heaps, and a tree's branches
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof from the משנה's words 'וכן בגת' (the same applies in a winepress). The proof tried to show that one may not stand in a רשות הרבים and drink from a כרמלית. רבא and רב ששת reject the proof: the line is about מעשר, and it follows רבי מאיר's view in a משנה about drinking at the winepress without tithing. A new משנה follows. It allows catching rainwater from a gutter but not pressing against it, because a gutter within three טפחים of the roof counts as the roof. Two ברייתות support this, and a תוספתא adds that a pipe four by four טפחים is its own domain. Next comes a משנה about drawing water from a cistern, or pouring water onto a garbage heap, through a window when the cistern or heap stands ten טפחים high in the street. רב הונא and רבי יוחנן explain the cistern case differently. The גמרא answers a worry that the heap may be removed by distinguishing a private heap from a public one. The amud ends with a משנה about carrying under a tree with drooping branches. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע limits that permission to בית סאתים, and the reason for the limit comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The winepress line as a proof about כרמלית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its proof from the משנה's words 'וכן בגת', reading the winepress as a כרמלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same applies in a winepress.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of the משנה, 'וכן בגת', as the final piece of its proof. This sets up the next move, where רבא will challenge this reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה already dealt with a רשות היחיד, so the winepress must be a different kind of place, a כרמלית. If the same rule applies there, then it is forbidden to stand in a רשות הרבים and drink from a כרמלית.

keyTerms.meaning: A winepress, the place where grapes are pressed into wine
An in-between domain on שבת, neither fully private nor fully public
And the same applies

phrases.english: And the same applies in a winepress.
phrases.notes: The גמרא reads this as being about a כרמלית on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof that began on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: That it is forbidden to stand in a רשות הרבים and drink from a כרמלית.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's words 'וכן בגת', read as describing a winepress that is a כרמלית.

steps.title: רבא says the winepress line is about tithes
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof by saying 'וכן בגת' is about מעשר, not שבת domains.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: it refers to the matter of tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down the proof by saying the winepress line has nothing to do with שבת. He says it is talking about the laws of מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On רבא's reading, 'וכן בגת' means that just as one must put his head and most of his body into the domain he drinks from, so too a person drinking at the winepress is exempt from מעשר only if his head and most of his body are in the winepress. This follows רבי מאיר in the משנה quoted below. Since the line is about tithing and not שבת domains, it proves nothing about a כרמלית.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding, with respect to the matter of
Tithe, the portion of produce that must be separated

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say the winepress is not a כרמלית. He only says the משנה's line is teaching a different law, so it cannot serve as a proof about שבת.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
It refers to the matter of tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in step 1.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the line is about שבת domains, but it is really about מעשר.

steps.title: רב ששת agrees with רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת independently explains 'וכן בגת' as being about מעשר, which supports רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly רב ששת said: 'And the same applies in a winepress' refers to the matter of tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב ששת read the משנה the same way רבא did. This strengthens רבא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the law. The גמרא is only showing that another אמורא already held this reading, which makes the rejection of the proof stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly [so-and-so] said, introducing someone who agrees

phrases.english: And similarly, Rav Sheshet said:
'And the same applies in a winepress' refers to the matter of tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's reading in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's reading that 'וכן בגת' is about מעשר.

steps.title: The source משנה: רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר בר צדוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה about drinking wine at the winepress without tithing. רבי מאיר exempts the drinker, and רבי אליעזר בר צדוק obligates him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: one may drink at the winepress, whether the wine is mixed with hot water or with cold water, and he is exempt from tithing. This is the view of רבי מאיר. רבי אליעזר בר צדוק obligates him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the tithing law about a winepress comes from. It quotes a משנה about drinking straight from the winepress before separating מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Casual drinking (אכילת עראי) is exempt from מעשר, but drinking that counts as a fixed meal (קבע) requires tithing. רבי מאיר says drinking at the winepress is always casual, whether the wine is mixed with hot or cold water. רבי אליעזר בר צדוק says it always requires tithing.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Hot water
Cold water
Exempt
Holds one obligated
Casual, incidental eating or drinking, which is exempt from מעשר

phrases.english: As we learned: one may drink on the winepress,
whether mixed with hot water or with cold water,
and he is exempt. These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Eliezer bar Tzadok obligates him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the tithing background that explains רבא's reading.
steps.raayaObject: That the winepress has its own tithing laws, which is what the משנה's 'וכן בגת' refers to.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about drinking at the winepress.

steps.title: The חכמים split between hot and cold
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that if the wine is mixed with hot water the drinker must tithe, but if it is mixed with cold water he is exempt, because he can pour the leftover back into the winepress.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: with hot water he is obligated, and with cold water he is exempt, because he returns the leftover.
steps.whatsHappening: The third opinion in the משנה makes a middle ruling. Whether the drinker must tithe depends on what the wine was mixed with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With cold water, the drinker can pour the leftover wine back into the press without ruining it, so his drinking stays casual and is exempt. With hot water, he cannot pour it back, because it would spoil the wine in the press. His drinking is then like a fixed meal (קבע), and he must tithe.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority view
Obligated
He returns, pours back
The leftover

steps.whatToRemember: רבא and רב ששת say 'וכן בגת' is about מעשר, not שבת, so it cannot prove anything about a כרמלית. The source is a three-way dispute: רבי מאיר always exempts, רבי אליעזר בר צדוק always obligates, and the חכמים exempt only with cold water, because the leftover can be poured back.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the key test for מעשר at the winepress. If the leftover can go back into the press, the drinking stays casual (עראי). If it cannot, the drinking counts as a fixed meal (קבע) and must be tithed.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
with hot water, he is obligated,
and with cold water, he is exempt,
because he returns the leftover.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third opinion in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine mixed with hot water requires tithing. Wine mixed with cold water is exempt, because the leftover can be poured back into the press.

steps.title: משנה: catching from a gutter and drinking from a pipe
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows catching water from a gutter below ten טפחים, and drinking from a pipe in any manner.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person may catch water from the gutter below ten handbreadths. From a pipe, he may drink in any manner.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets two rules: from a gutter you may only catch the water, but from a pipe you may drink any way you like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the gutter and the pipe differently. With the gutter, the wording 'catch' is limited. With the pipe, the phrase 'in any manner' means even putting your mouth right on it is allowed. The גמרא will now ask why the gutter is more limited.

keyTerms.meaning: Catches (water as it falls, without touching the source)
A gutter running along the edge of a roof
A pipe or spout sticking out from the roof
In any manner, with no restriction
Ten handbreadths, the height that marks the limit of a public domain

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A person may catch water from the gutter
below ten handbreadths;
and from the pipe, he may drink in any manner.
phrases.notes: 'In any manner' means even pressing his mouth directly to the pipe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of drinking wine at the winepress.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From a gutter one may catch water below ten טפחים. From a pipe one may drink in any manner.

steps.title: Reading the משנה: catching yes, pressing no — why?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that pressing against the gutter is forbidden and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: To catch the water, yes. But to press against the gutter, no. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה's word 'catch' closely and concludes that pressing against the gutter is not allowed. It then asks why, which sets up רב נחמן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'catch' about the gutter but 'any manner' about the pipe. That contrast shows that pressing against the gutter is forbidden. The question is what makes touching the gutter a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Presses or joins (putting hand or mouth right up against the gutter)
Yes
What is the reason?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
To catch — yes;
but to press against it — no.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: קוֹלֵט — אִין, אֲבָל מְצָרֵף — לָא. מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה's wording and asks for its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is pressing against the gutter forbidden when catching from it is allowed?

steps.title: רב נחמן: the gutter counts as part of the roof
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains that the gutter is within three טפחים of the roof, so it is treated like the roof itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Here we are dealing with a gutter that is less than three handbreadths from the roof. Anything less than three handbreadths from the roof is treated like the roof.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question. The gutter is so close to the roof that it counts as part of the roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the gap is less than three טפחים, the gutter is treated as joined to the roof. Pressing against the gutter is therefore like taking water directly from the roof, which is a different domain. Catching water after it has fallen away from the gutter does not count as taking from the roof.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than three handbreadths
Close to the roof
It is considered like the roof
We are dealing with

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not the water itself. The problem is that touching the gutter counts as touching the roof, because the gutter is within three טפחים of it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the rule that a gap of less than three טפחים is treated as closed. That rule is the key to the whole משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
Here, with a gutter less than three handbreadths
from the roof we are dealing;
for anything less than three handbreadths from the roof
is considered like the roof.
phrases.notes: This is based on the principle of לבוד: a gap of less than three is treated as closed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הָכָא בְּמַזְחֵילָה פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה סָמוּךְ לַגַּג עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The gutter is within three טפחים of the roof, so it counts as the roof. Pressing against it is like taking directly from the roof's domain.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the rule: catch, but do not press
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one may raise his hand near the roof and catch water, as long as he does not press against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: A person may stand in a private domain and raise his hand above ten handbreadths, to within three handbreadths of the roof, and catch water, as long as he does not press against it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the difference between catching and pressing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when the hand is right near the roof, catching is allowed. Only pressing is forbidden. This matches what we learned from the משנה and from רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא that supports what was just said)
A private domain
As long as / provided that

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
A person may stand in a private domain
and raise his hand above ten handbreadths
to within three handbreadths of the roof,
and catch water, provided that he does not press against it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the distinction between catching and pressing drawn in steps 7–8.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that catching is allowed but pressing near the roof is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that allows catching within three טפחים of the roof, but not pressing.

steps.title: A second ברייתא says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא forbids pressing against the roof area but allows catching and drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: A person should not stand in a private domain, raise his hand above ten handbreadths to within three of the roof, and press against it. But he may catch the water and drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא with the same rule, phrased the other way around: first what is forbidden, then what is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא started with what is allowed. This one starts with what is forbidden. Together they make the rule clear: pressing is forbidden, catching is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Another ברייתא taught
And drinks

steps.whatToRemember: Water from a gutter within three טפחים of the roof may be caught and drunk. But you may not press your hand or mouth against the gutter, because it counts as part of the roof.

phrases.english: Another baraita taught:
A person may not stand in a private domain
and raise his hand above ten handbreadths
to within three handbreadths of the roof and press against it;
but he may catch the water and drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second supporting ברייתא with the same rule.
steps.raayaObject: The distinction between pressing (forbidden) and catching (allowed).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A second ברייתא that forbids pressing near the roof but allows catching and drinking.

steps.title: A wide pipe counts as its own domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'from a pipe one may drink in any manner,' then brings a תנא who limits that rule: if the pipe is four by four טפחים, drinking by pressing against it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: From a pipe, one may drink in any manner. It was taught: if the pipe is four by four handbreadths, it is forbidden, because he is like one who carries from one domain to another domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה about the pipe. It then brings a teaching that puts a limit on that line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pipe sticks out more than three טפחים from the roof, so it is not treated like the roof. That is why the משנה lets a person drink from it in any manner, even pressing his mouth or hand against it. But if the pipe is four by four טפחים, it is a significant place and counts as a separate רשות, so taking water straight from it is like carrying from one רשות to another.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was taught.' This introduces a teaching of the תנאים from outside the משנה, here from the תוספתא.
A pipe or spout that sticks out from the roof.
Four by four טפחים. This is the minimum size for a place to count as its own domain.
Carrying from one domain to another, which is forbidden on שבת.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this contradicts the משנה. 'In any manner' is the general rule for an ordinary pipe. The תנא only adds an exception for a pipe large enough (four by four) to be its own רשות.

phrases.english: From a pipe, one may drink in any manner.
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the words of the משנה.

phrases.english: It was taught: if the pipe has
phrases.notes: This is a תוספתא.

phrases.english: four by four handbreadths, it is forbidden,
phrases.notes: Forbidden to press against it and drink.

phrases.english: because he is like one who carries
from one domain to another domain.
phrases.notes: The pipe counts as its own domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אִם יֵשׁ בְּצִינּוֹר אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the gutter (steps 7–10), the גמרא turns to the משנה's second clause about the pipe and limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ordinary pipe may be drunk from in any manner, but a pipe that is four by four טפחים is its own domain, so pressing against it to drink is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the size of a place (four by four) can turn it into its own רשות. This idea comes back throughout מסכת עירובין.

steps.title: Drawing water from a cistern through a window
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a cistern in the public domain has an embankment ten טפחים high. One may draw water from it on שבת through a window that sits above it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A cistern in the public domain whose embankment is ten handbreadths high, and a window is above it: one may draw water from it on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a person may draw water through his window from a cistern standing in the public street, if the cistern's embankment is ten טפחים high.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An embankment ten טפחים high makes the cistern area a רשות היחיד of its own, even though it stands in רשות הרבים. The house with the window is also a private domain. So drawing water from the cistern into the house is moving from private domain to private domain, which is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Our משנה.' This marks the start of a new משנה.
A cistern or pit that holds water.
The raised rim or embankment around the cistern.
The public domain.
'They may draw' (fill up) water.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A cistern in the public domain
and its embankment is ten handbreadths high,
phrases.notes: This height makes it a private domain.

phrases.english: a window that is above it:
phrases.notes: The window of a nearby house.

phrases.english: one may draw water from it on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic: windows over private domains that stand inside the public domain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may draw water on שבת through a window from a cistern in רשות הרבים whose embankment is ten טפחים high.

steps.title: Pouring water onto a garbage pile through a window
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues with a second case: a garbage pile ten טפחים high in the public domain. One may pour water onto it on שבת from a window above it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A garbage pile in the public domain that is ten handbreadths high, and a window is above it: one may pour water onto it on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a parallel case. This time water goes out from the house onto a high garbage pile in the street.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works by the same logic as the cistern. A pile ten טפחים high counts as a private domain, so pouring from the house onto it moves from private domain to private domain. The only change is the direction: in the cistern case water comes in, and here water goes out.

keyTerms.meaning: A garbage or trash pile.
'They may pour.'
A window.

steps.whatToRemember: Both cases in the משנה rest on one rule: something ten טפחים high in the street counts as a private domain. So a window above it may move things to it or from it.

phrases.english: A garbage pile in the public domain
that is ten handbreadths high,
phrases.notes: So it counts as a private domain.

phrases.english: a window that is above it:
one may pour water onto it on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁפָּה בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים גְּבוֹהָ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second case of the same משנה, parallel to the cistern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may pour water on שבת from a window onto a garbage pile in רשות הרבים that is ten טפחים high.

steps.title: What setup is the cistern case talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exact situation the משנה means. It tests the first option, a cistern right next to the wall, and challenges it: then why would the משנה need an embankment ten טפחים high?
steps.simpleTranslation: With what are we dealing? If you say it is a cistern right next to the wall, why do I need the embankment to be ten handbreadths?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to figure out the exact setup of the משנה. It rejects the first possibility right away, which sets up the answers in steps 15 and 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cistern is right next to the house wall (less than four טפחים away), no public traffic passes between them. The cistern itself is ten טפחים deep, so it is already a private domain. If so, drawing should be allowed even without a high embankment, and the משנה's demand for a ten-טפחים embankment seems pointless. רב הונא will answer by moving the cistern away from the wall (step 15). רבי יוחנן will keep the adjacent case and reread the 'ten' (step 17).

keyTerms.meaning: 'With what are we dealing?' The גמרא asks for the exact case the משנה means.
'If you say.' This opens a possibility that the גמרא is about to reject.
Adjacent, meaning right next to the wall (less than four טפחים away).
'Why do I need?' This points out that a detail would be unnecessary.

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not challenging the ruling of the משנה itself. It is only showing that the 'right next to the wall' setup cannot be what the משנה means, because then the embankment detail would be unnecessary.

phrases.english: GEMARA: With what are we dealing?
If you say it is adjacent to the wall,
phrases.notes: Within four טפחים of the house.

phrases.english: why do I need the embankment to be ten?
phrases.notes: The cistern's depth would already make it a private domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בִּסְמוּכָה, לְמָה לִי חוּלְיָא עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens its analysis of the new משנה by asking what exact setup it means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact physical setup of the cistern in the משנה: is it right next to the wall or set apart from it?
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that the cistern is adjacent to the house wall.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the cistern is adjacent, its own depth of ten טפחים already makes it a private domain with no public traffic in between. So the משנה's requirement of a ten-טפחים embankment would be pointless.

steps.title: רב הונא: The cistern is four handbreadths away from the wall
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers the question from Step 14. The משנה is talking about a cistern that stands four טפחים away from the house's wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: What case are we dealing with here? A cistern that is four handbreadths away from the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question of Step 14 by saying the cistern is not right next to the wall. It stands four טפחים away from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 asked: if the cistern touches the wall, why does the משנה need a ten-טפחים embankment? רב הונא answers by placing the cistern four טפחים away. That gap is a real strip of רשות הרבים between the house and the cistern, and the embankment matters because of that gap.

keyTerms.meaning: "What case are we dealing with here?" A formula that opens a narrow definition of the case.
Separated, at a distance from
Wall (here, the wall of the house with the window)

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
With what are we dealing here?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is about to explain the משנה as talking about one specific case.

phrases.english: With a cistern that is four handbreadths removed from the wall.
phrases.notes: Four טפחים is enough for the gap to count as a real piece of the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14 by choosing a different placement for the cistern.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What physical setup does the משנה describe, so that the ten-טפחים embankment is needed?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cistern stands four טפחים away from the wall, so there is public domain in between.

steps.title: Why the ten-handbreadth embankment is needed in רב הונא's case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how רב הונא's reading works. The embankment lets the water pass high enough. Without it, a person would be carrying from one private domain to another through the public domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the reason it is permitted is that there is an embankment of ten handbreadths. But if there is no embankment of ten, he would be carrying from a private domain to a private domain by way of the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the logic behind רב הונא's answer. It shows exactly what the ten-טפחים embankment accomplishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The house is a רשות היחיד, and the cistern is also a private area. Between them lies a strip of רשות הרבים. If the embankment is ten טפחים high, the bucket travels above ten טפחים, which is above the public domain's airspace and therefore allowed. Without that height, the bucket would pass through the public domain itself, and carrying between two private domains through public space is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason
Carries or moves an object
Private domain
Public domain

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the problem here is carrying into the public domain and leaving the object there. The water never stays in the public area. The issue is only that it travels through the public domain on its way between two private domains.

phrases.english: And the reason is that there is an embankment of ten,
phrases.notes: Ten טפחים is the height at which the public domain's airspace ends.

phrases.english: but if there is no embankment of ten —

phrases.aramaic: קָא מְטַלְטֵל מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לִרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד
phrases.english: he would be carrying from a private domain to a private domain
by way of the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטַעְמָא דְּאִיכָּא חוּלְיָא עֲשָׂרָה, הָא לֵיכָּא חוּלְיָא עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and completes the logic of רב הונא's answer in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב הונא's case, drawing water is permitted only because the ten-טפחים embankment lifts the transfer above the public domain. Without it, the transfer is forbidden as carrying between private domains through public space.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Even next to the wall, the depth and the embankment add up to ten
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer. The cistern can even be right next to the wall. The משנה's point is that the cistern's depth and its embankment combine to make up the ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: You can even say the cistern is adjacent to the wall. The משנה is teaching us that a cistern and its embankment combine to make ten.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן offers a second way to answer the question of Step 14. He keeps the simple case of a cistern touching the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 asked why an embankment is needed if the cistern touches the wall. רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה's 'ten' is not the embankment's height alone. It is the cistern's depth plus the embankment together. The lesson of the משנה is that these two measurements can be added together to reach ten טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: Adjacent, right next to (the wall)
"This is what it teaches us": identifies the new lesson of a source
Cistern, a pit for water
Combine, add up together

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of the cistern case. רב הונא says the cistern is four טפחים from the wall, and the embankment lifts the transfer above the public domain. רבי יוחנן says the cistern is next to the wall, and the depth and embankment combine to reach ten.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even if you say it is adjacent to the wall —
phrases.notes: He accepts the very case that Step 14 had trouble with.

phrases.english: this is what it teaches us:
that a cistern and its embankment combine to make ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בִּסְמוּכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to רב הונא's (Steps 15-16) for the same question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The question of Step 14: why the משנה needs an embankment of ten if the cistern touches the wall.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting what the משנה's measurement refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the embankment itself had to be ten טפחים high, which seemed pointless if the cistern touched the wall.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ten is a combined measurement. The cistern's depth and its embankment together reach ten, and that combining is the new lesson.

steps.title: The garbage pile: Shouldn't we worry it might be removed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's second case, the garbage pile in the public domain. It challenges the case: shouldn't we worry that the pile will be taken away?
steps.simpleTranslation: A garbage pile in the public domain, etc. But aren't we worried that the garbage pile might be removed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the second case of the משנה (from Step 13) and raises a challenge against permitting it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows pouring water onto a ten-טפחים garbage pile, because the pile counts as a private area. But a garbage pile is not permanent, since people may clear it away. If it is removed, the spot becomes ordinary public domain. Someone used to pouring water there might keep doing so, which would put water into the רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned, we worry (about a possible problem)
Will be taken away, removed

phrases.english: "A garbage pile in the public domain," etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, introducing the next discussion.

phrases.english: But are we not concerned that the garbage pile might be removed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the cistern discussion and opens a new challenge on the משנה's second case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to pour water from a window onto a ten-טפחים garbage pile in the public domain.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A garbage pile is temporary. If it is removed, the spot becomes public domain, and people used to pouring there may keep pouring water into the רשות הרבים.

steps.title: The incident of the alley between the sea and a garbage heap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a story from רבי יצחק. רבי refused to rule either way on an alley bounded by the sea and a garbage heap.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבין בר רב אדא say in the name of רבי יצחק: there was a case of an alley where one side ended at the sea and the other side ended at a garbage heap. The case came before רבי, and he said neither that it was forbidden nor that it was permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that seems to show we really do worry a garbage heap might be removed. This strengthens the challenge from Step 18 against our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה treats a garbage heap in the public domain as a solid enough partition. But in this story רבי would not permit carrying when one side of an alley was closed only by a garbage heap. That suggests a heap is not a trustworthy partition, so the story clashes with the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But surely...' A formula that brings a source to contradict what was just said
An incident, a real case that happened
An alleyway that opens onto the public domain
Ends at the sea, meaning the sea closes off that side
Neither prohibition nor permission. רבי gave no ruling

phrases.english: But didn't Ravin bar Rav Adda
say that Rabbi Yitzchak said:
There was an incident with a certain alleyway
one of whose sides ended at the sea
and whose other side ended at a garbage heap
and the incident came before Rebbi
and he did not say about it
either prohibition or permission.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and sharpens the challenge in Step 18 with a story about a garbage heap used as a partition.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a garbage heap in the public domain works as a partition ten טפחים high.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי would not permit carrying when an alley relied on a garbage heap, which shows a heap is suspect because it might be removed. So why does the משנה rely on one?

steps.title: Why רבי did not permit
steps.stepSummary: רבי did not permit carrying because the heap might be removed and the sea might pull back behind a strip of sediment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not say it was permitted, because we worry that the garbage heap might be taken away, and that the sea might throw up sediment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of רבי's silence: why he would not permit carrying in the alley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both partitions are unstable. Someone could take away the heap. The sea could leave a strip of sediment that opens a gap between the alley and the water. Either way the alley could lose a partition, so רבי would not give a permission.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned, we take the possibility into account
Lest it be taken away
Sediment or silt the sea throws up onto the shore, which pushes the water back

phrases.english: He did not say it was permitted
because we are concerned lest the garbage heap be removed
and lest the sea throw up sediment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 'no permission' half of רבי's silence in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We worry that a garbage heap may be removed and that the sea may recede, so carrying in such an alley cannot be permitted outright.

steps.title: Why רבי did not forbid
steps.stepSummary: רבי did not forbid carrying because, right now, the partitions are actually standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not say it was forbidden, because the partitions really do exist.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of רבי's silence: why he would not forbid carrying either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the moment, the sea and the heap really do close off the alley, so carrying there is technically fine. רבי could not call it forbidden. He could only refuse to permit it because of the worry about the future. The upshot for our סוגיא is that a garbage heap is a real partition, but we do worry it might be removed.

keyTerms.meaning: They are standing, they exist
Partitions, walls that close off an area

phrases.english: He did not say it was prohibited
because the partitions do exist.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of רבי's silence begun in Step 20, and finishes setting up the contradiction with the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the partitions are actually standing now, carrying cannot be called forbidden.

steps.title: A private heap versus a public heap
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. The heap in רבי's case belonged to one person, and he might remove it. The heap in our משנה is public and will stay where it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. This case, the story, is about a private heap. That case, our משנה, is about a public heap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Steps 18-21 by showing that the two cases involve different kinds of garbage heaps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual owns a private heap and could change his mind and clear it away, so we worry it will disappear. No single person controls a public heap, so in practice it stays put and we do not worry. That is why our משנה can rely on a heap in the public domain.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. A formula that introduces a resolution of a contradiction
Belonging to an individual, a private heap
Belonging to the public, a public heap

steps.whatToRemember: A garbage heap counts as a partition. We worry that a private heap might be removed, but a public heap is treated as permanent, so the משנה's heap in the public domain is reliable.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the story proves that a garbage heap is never a partition. רבי admitted the partitions were valid. He only worried that a private heap might be removed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a general principle: how much we trust a partition depends on whether one person can easily remove it. That affects which barriers you can rely on for carrying on שבת.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This case is about a private heap
and that case is about a public heap.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּיָחִיד, הָא דְּרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction between our משנה and the story of רבי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (אוקימתא): the two sources deal with different kinds of garbage heaps.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought every garbage heap is suspect, because someone might remove it, as in רבי's case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a private heap is suspect. A public heap is considered permanent, so the משנה can rely on it as a partition.

steps.title: Carrying under a tree whose branches hang down
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a tree's drooping branches reach to within three טפחים of the ground, one may carry under it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a tree hangs down over the ground, and its branches are less than three handbreadths above the ground, you may carry under it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes a tree whose branches hang down all around like a tent, and it rules that you may carry underneath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap of less than three טפחים is treated as closed (לבוד). So the hanging branches count as solid walls around the area under the tree. That makes the space an enclosed private area, and carrying there is allowed even if the tree stands in a public place.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marked מַתְנִי׳)
A tree
Hanging over, covering like a tent
Three handbreadths, the key height in this law
One may carry or move objects

steps.confusionAlert: Here גּוּפוֹ does not mean the tree trunk. It means the drooping branches, which must come down to within three טפחים of the ground so they can act as walls.
steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the rule of לבוד: a gap of under three טפחים counts as closed. That rule is what turns branches into walls.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A tree that was hanging over the ground,
phrases.notes: Its branches droop down on all sides like a tent.

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵין גּוּפוֹ גָּבוֹהַּ מִן הָאָרֶץ
phrases.english: if its body (the hanging branches) is not higher from the ground
than three handbreadths,
one may carry under it.
phrases.notes: The branches work as partitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the garbage-heap discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If drooping branches come to within three טפחים of the ground, they count as walls, and one may carry under the tree.

steps.title: Not sitting on raised tree roots
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that roots rising three טפחים above the ground may not be sat on during שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the tree's roots stick up three handbreadths above the ground, you may not sit on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second rule about the same tree. This one is about its roots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a tree on שבת is forbidden by the חכמים. Roots that rise three טפחים or more above the ground count as part of the tree, so sitting on them is using the tree. Roots lower than that count as ground and are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Roots
High, raised up
One may not sit

phrases.english: If its roots are higher than the ground
by three handbreadths,
one may not sit on them.
phrases.notes: Using a tree on שבת is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׇׁרָשָׁיו גְּבוֹהִים מִן הָאָרֶץ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling in the same משנה about the same tree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roots three טפחים above the ground have the status of the tree, so one may not sit on them on שבת.

steps.title: Carrying under the tree is limited to בית סאתים
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע limits the משנה's permission: one may not carry under the tree if the area is more than בית סאתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב הונא, the son of רב יהושע, said: You may not carry under the tree if the area is bigger than בית סאתים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and quotes an אמורא who puts a size limit on the משנה's permission to carry under the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה did not mention any size limit. רב הונא adds one: if the area under the branches is bigger than בית סאתים, carrying is forbidden. The tree's 'walls' work, but only for an area up to that size.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה (marked גְּמָ׳)
רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, an אמורא
An area for sowing two סאה of seed, about 5,000 square אמות
More than

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
One may not carry in it (under the tree)
if it is more than two beit se'a,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה's first ruling with a size limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying under the tree is allowed only if the area is no more than בית סאתים.

steps.title: Asking the reason for the size limit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב הונא limits the area under the tree to בית סאתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב הונא's rule. This is a setup line, and the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The branches do form proper walls, so it is not obvious why the size of the area should matter. The גמרא wants to know what makes this enclosure different and limited to בית סאתים.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רב הונא's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why carrying under a tree is limited to an area of בית סאתים.
